entries.test: Public evidence on OpenAI's technology, sustained adoption, internal tensions, profitability, and competitive advantages through July 24, 2024 would test whether the January warnings had borne out.
entries.note: This is a compound claim; each component needs evidence.

entries.test: Contemporaneous usage, retention, and production deployment data would show the extent of sustained OpenAI adoption by July 24, 2024.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion concerns OpenAI; the proposition broadens adoption to all generative AI.

entries.test: Comparative benchmarks and capability evaluations of OpenAI technology available in January and July 2024 would show whether significant improvement occurred.
entries.note: The proposition turns a statement about OpenAI's progress into a universal statement about LLM technology.

entries.test: OpenAI's release announcements and public product availability would establish whether GPT-5 had been released by July 24, 2024.
entries.note: The cutoff is the publication date.
He reports a longstanding suspicion about losses; the proposition recasts that as a present probability assessment.
The explanation attributes a private motive for financial nondisclosure. Losses and disclosure practices alone would not establish that motive.

entries.test: Anthropic's contemporaneous financial reporting and public disclosures would establish its losses and whether it disclosed costs and profits.
entries.note: The proposition makes the tentative comparison more categorical and specific than 'similar challenges' warrants.

entries.test: Public evidence of switching costs, exclusive assets, network effects, and durable technological or cost advantages would test whether OpenAI had a competitive moat beyond its brand in July 2024.
entries.note: The proposition omits 'as far as I can tell.' The post gives moat a concrete competitive meaning.

entries.test: Provider migration evidence, competing model prices, OpenAI's July 2024 price changes, and contemporaneous reporting would test whether cheaper alternatives drove those cuts.
entries.note: This combines a switching-cost observation with a causal claim about pricing.

entries.test: Meta's release terms and benchmark results, together with evidence of customer substitution and pressure on OpenAI's business, would test the claimed competitive damage.
entries.note: The sentence attributes business damage to Meta's free offering. Its metaphor has a concrete competitive reading.

entries.test: July 2024 model availability, pricing, performance comparisons, and switching costs would show whether comparable LLM offerings were interchangeable and available free.
entries.note: The preceding discussion supplies a plain reading of commodity as substitutable competing offerings.

entries.test: Public fundraising announcements and reporting would establish whether OpenAI sought additional cash, while financial evidence would test its dependence on external funding for survival.
entries.note: Subsequent public fundraising events can settle the predicted attempt by the evaluation date. The exclusive survival claim requires separate financial evidence.
Both 'may be fatal' and 'may well' express possibility rather than a firm prediction.
'Ditto' extends the preceding possibility of fatal competitive pressure to Anthropic and others.
